section.title: Activity
section.para: The expressions \(p(200 − 5p)\) and \(-5p^2 + 200p\) define the same function. The function models the revenue a school would earn from selling raffle tickets at \(p\) dollars each.

div.para: $0 and $40. For example, if the equation \(p(200−5p)=0\) is true, then either \(p\) is equal to 0, or \(200−5p\) is equal to 0. If \(200−5p=0\), then \(p\) is 40, because \(200−5(40)\) is 0.

list.item: At what price or prices would the school collect $0 revenue from raffle sales? Explain or show your reasoning.

div.para: We could write \(p(200 − 5p) = 500\) and \(-5p^2 + 200p = 500\). Approximate solutions can be found using trial and error or graphing. However, we don’t yet know an exact way to solve either equation.

list.item: The school staff noticed that there are two ticket prices that would result in a revenue of $500. What equation could you use to determine what those two prices are?

div.para: Moving the same distance away from each horizontal intercept, at $0 and $40, results in equal revenue. This means $10 and $30 earn an equal amount of revenue.

problem.title: Extending Your Thinking
problem.para: Can you find the following prices without graphing?

list.item: If the school charges $10, it will collect $1500 in revenue. Find another price that would generate $1500 in revenue.

div.para: Moving the same distance away from each horizontal intercept, at $0 and $40, results in equal revenue. This means $12 and $28 earn an equal amount of revenue.

list.item: If the school charges $28, it will collect $1680 in revenue. Find another price that would generate $1680 in revenue.

div.para: $20. Moving the same distance away from each horizontal intercept results in equal revenue. The farther away we move from one horizontal intercept in the direction of the other intercept, the greater the revenue. An optimal ticket price of $20, producing $2000 in revenue, is found in the middle point between the two intercepts, at \(p = 20\).

list.item: Find the price that would produce the maximum possible revenue. Be prepared to show your reasoning.
